Our strengths include frontend development, UI/UX design, research and problem-solving. Our team lead has national-level hackathon experience through AeroLift BlackBox, selected for Robofest. summary:
(R&B) Round & Blues: The Earth Information Jukebox transforms NASA Earth science visualizations into immersive sound experiences through data sonification. It explores how visual patterns and environmental changes can be translated into audio features such as pitch, rhythm, and intensity, allowing users to experience Earth science through both sight and sound.

Users can explore selected Earth visualizations, experience corresponding soundscapes, and discover patterns in complex environmental information through an additional sensory channel. By combining interactive visualization, data processing, and audio synthesis, R&B aims to make Earth science more engaging and accessible, particularly for blind and low-vision audiences.

Our vision is to evolve the platform beyond sonification by incorporating historical data analysis and predictive models, enabling users to explore not only observed environmental changes but also potential future trends through sound.
details:
R&B — Round & Blues: The Earth Information Jukebox

What We Developed

R&B is an interactive Earth-science sonification platform that transforms NASA Earth visualizations into corresponding sound experiences. It aims to provide an additional way to explore complex environmental information by combining visual and auditory representations.

Users can select an Earth-science visualization and experience a soundscape generated by mapping visual or data features to audio properties. Features such as brightness, color, density, movement, and variation is translated into sound characteristics such as pitch, rhythm, intensity, and modulation.

How It Works

The platform follows a five-stage workflow:

  1. Select a Visualization: Choose an Earth-science visualization from the available collection.
  2. Hover to Listen: Move your cursor over different geographical locations to hear corresponding audio variations.
  3. Select a Region: Click on a geographical region to open its focused visualization.
  4. Explore the Soundscape: Listen to how the sound changes according to the selected region and its visualized features.
  5. Discover Earth Through Sound: Experience geographical and environmental variations through synchronized visual and auditory representations.

NASA Data and Scientific Relevance

The project explores NASA Earth-observation visualizations covering ocean circulation, sea-surface temperature, lightning, nighttime lights, atmospheric composition, carbon dioxide, forest structure, and atmospheric rivers. These examples demonstrate how different Earth systems can be experienced through sound.

Benefits and Intended Impact

R&B aims to:

  • Make complex Earth-science information more engaging and approachable.
  • Provide an additional sensory channel for exploring environmental patterns.
  • Support more inclusive science communication, particularly for blind and low-vision audiences.
  • Create opportunities for multisensory learning in schools, universities, museums, and public science outreach.
  • Help users notice changes and relationships in environmental information through listening as well as viewing.

Technology Used

The project was developed using web technologies, including Next.js, React, TypeScript, D3-Geo, HTML5 Canvas, and the Web Audio API. The platform uses browser-based audio generation and playback alongside interactive Earth visualization.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The central creative idea is to treat sound as an additional interface for Earth science rather than simply background audio. The mappings are intended to communicate meaningful features of the selected visualization. The team also considered scientific interpretability, accessibility, audio clarity, performance, browser compatibility, and the need to explain what each sound represents.

Future Scope

Our long-term vision is to evolve R&B into a predictive planetary observatory. Future development could incorporate historical and near-real-time Earth-observation datasets, trend analysis, and suitable forecasting models to estimate possible future environmental conditions. These projected outcomes could then be represented through distinct soundscapes, allowing users to listen to both observed changes and potential future scenarios.

Predictive forecasting is a proposed future capability, not a feature claimed to be implemented in the current prototype. Any future predictions would need scientific validation, uncertainty communication, and transparent data sources.
